steps: Rinse the spinach in cold water, lift it out and dry it completely in a salad spinner or between clean kitchen towels. Wet leaves make the dressing slide off and the salad soggy.
Toast the pecans in a dry frying pan on medium heat for 2 min, stirring constantly, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool, then break each one in half.
Wash the strawberries, pull off the green tops with a small knife and cut each berry into thin slices from top to bottom.
Make the dressing: put the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey and a pinch of salt and pepper in a small jar. Close the lid and shake hard for 15 seconds until it looks creamy and combined.
Put the spinach in a large bowl and drizzle over about half of the dressing. Toss gently with your hands so every leaf is lightly coated.
Add the strawberries and most of the pecans, crumble in the feta with your fingers and toss once more, very gently so the berries do not get crushed.
Taste a leaf and add more salt, pepper or dressing if needed. Scatter the remaining pecans on top and serve right away.
Take the pork out of the fridge 20 min before cooking so it cooks evenly. Heat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the baby potatoes in half and toss them on a baking tray with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper and the herb sprigs. Roast for 25 min, until golden and a knife slides in easily.
Pat the pork very dry with paper towels and season both sides generously with salt and pepper. Dry meat browns, wet meat steams.
When the potatoes have 10 min left, toss the broccolini with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 sliced garlic clove and a pinch of salt, then add it to the tray.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a heavy frying pan on high heat until it just starts to smoke. Lay in the steaks and do not move them. Sear for 4 min until deep golden brown, flip and sear 4 min on the other side.

Turn the heat to low, add the butter and 2 crushed garlic cloves and spoon the foaming butter over the pork for 1 min. It is done when the centre reaches 63°C, or when the juices run clear with only a hint of pink.
Move the pork to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 min so the juices stay inside the meat.
Serve the pork with the potatoes and broccolini and spoon the pan juices over the top.
Cut the tomatoes into quarters and cut out the hard white core. Chop the onion finely and peel and slice the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot on medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 6 min, stirring, until soft and see-through but not brown.
Add the garlic and stir for 1 min until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down, partly cover and simmer for 20 min until the tomatoes are completely soft and falling apart.
Turn off the heat. Blend with a hand blender in the pot, or pour carefully into a blender in batches, filling it only halfway to avoid hot splashes. Blend until completely smooth.
Return to low heat and stir in 80ml of the cream and half the torn basil. Season with salt and pepper. If it is too thick add a splash of hot water, and if it is too sharp add another pinch of sugar.
Ladle into bowls, swirl in the rest of the cream, add the remaining basil and a grind of black pepper. Serve with toasted bread.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the cauliflower into small bite-size florets. Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then pat them very dry with a clean towel so they turn crisp.
On the tray toss the cauliflower and chickpeas with 2 tbsp olive oil, the cumin, paprika and 1 tsp salt. Spread in a single layer with space between pieces, using two trays if needed.
Roast for 25 min, turning everything once halfway, until the cauliflower has brown edges and the chickpeas are crisp.
Meanwhile cut the pomegranate in half. Hold one half cut side down over a bowl and hit the back firmly with a wooden spoon until the seeds fall out. Pick out any white skin.
Make the dressing by squeezing the juice of the lemon into a small bowl and whisking in 1 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Let the roasted vegetables cool for 5 min. Mix with the spinach, pomegranate seeds and chopped parsley, pour over the dressing, toss gently and serve.
Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp salt and bring to a rolling boil. Meanwhile peel and thinly slice the garlic and grate the parmesan.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan on low heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 min until fragrant but not brown. Burnt garlic turns bitter.
Pour in the passata and add the sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 10 min, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Cook the ravioli in the boiling water for about 4 min, or follow the packet. They are ready when they float to the top. Scoop out a cup of pasta water before draining.
Lift the ravioli straight into the sauce with a slotted spoon. Tipping them into a colander can break them. Add a splash of pasta water and turn gently for 1 min so the sauce coats every piece.
Tear the basil over the top, add the parmesan and a grind of pepper and serve at once.
Switch on the waffle iron to preheat and brush it lightly with oil or melted butter.
Melt the butter in the microwave for 30 seconds or in a small pan, then let it cool a little so it does not scramble the eggs.
In a large bowl whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In a jug whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla until combined.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir with a spatula just until combined. Lumps are fine, and over-mixing makes tough waffles. Fold in most of the pecans and rest the batter for 5 min.
Pour about one ladleful of batter into the centre of the iron and close the lid. Cook for 4 min until the steam slows and the waffle is golden. Do not open early or it will tear.
Lift the waffle out with a fork and keep it on a wire rack in a 100°C oven so it stays crisp. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Stack the waffles, sprinkle with the remaining pecans and drizzle with maple syrup.
Cut the paneer into 2cm cubes and soak in warm salted water for 10 min to keep it soft. Roughly chop the onion and tomatoes.
Heat the oil and 1 tbsp butter in a pan. Fry the paneer for 1 min per side until lightly golden, then lift out and set aside.
In the same pan cook the onion for 5 min until soft. Add the ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 min until the raw smell goes.
Add the tomatoes, cashews, 100ml water, chilli powder and 1 tsp salt. Cover and cook for 10 min until the tomatoes are mushy.
Let the mixture cool for 5 min, then blend until silky smooth.
Pour the sauce back into the pan on low heat. Add the remaining butter, sugar and garam masala and simmer for 5 min, adding a splash of water if it is too thick.
Add the paneer and cream and simmer for 2 min. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and sprinkle it in. Serve with naan or rice.

ing: 3 tbsp warm milk with a pinch of saffron
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water 4 to 5 times until the water runs almost clear, then soak it in fresh water for 30 min.
Slice the onions thinly and fry in the oil on medium heat for 15 min, stirring often, until deep golden and crisp. Lift out half onto a plate for the topping and leave the rest in the pot.
Chop the vegetables to a similar size. Mix them with the yoghurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, half the mint and coriander, the slit chillies and 1 tsp salt. Leave for 20 min.
Boil 2 litres of water with the bay leaf, cardamom, cloves and 2 tbsp salt. Drain the rice and add it. Cook for 5 min only, until it is about 70% cooked and still firm in the middle, then drain.
Spread the marinated vegetables in the pot with the leftover onions to make the base layer.
Cover the vegetables with the rice and scatter over the crispy onions, the rest of the mint and coriander and the saffron milk.
Cover with a tight lid, sealing the edge with foil or dough. Heat on high until steam escapes, then turn to the lowest heat and cook 20 min. Do not lift the lid.
Turn off the heat and rest for 5 min. Gently mix from the edges so the layers blend and serve with raita.

ing: Coconut chutney and sambar to serve
steps: Take the batter out of the fridge 30 min before cooking. It should be pourable like thin pancake batter, so add water 1 tbsp at a time if it is thick. Stir in 1 tsp salt.
Boil the whole potatoes for 15 min until soft. Cool, peel and roughly mash with a fork, leaving small chunks.

Make the filling: heat the oil and add the mustard seeds. When they pop, add the curry leaves, chopped chillies and sliced onion and cook for 5 min until soft. Stir in the turmeric, salt, potatoes and 3 tbsp water and mix for 2 min. Keep warm.
Heat a flat non-stick pan or tawa on medium-high for 2 min until a drop of water sizzles and vanishes. Wipe the surface with half an onion or an oiled cloth.
Pour a ladleful of batter into the centre. Using the bottom of the ladle, spread it outward in circles as thin as you can.
Drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge. Cook for 2 min without flipping, until the underside is deep golden and the top looks dry.
Spoon the filling in a line across the middle and fold both sides over, or roll it up. Serve at once with chutney and sambar.
Wipe the pan, stir the batter and repeat. The first dosa often tears, which is normal.
Put a baking tray or pizza stone on the top shelf and heat the oven to its highest setting, up to 250°C, for 30 min. A very hot tray gives a crisp base.
While the oven heats, leave the dough covered at room temperature so it becomes soft and stretchy.
Stir a pinch of salt and 1 tsp olive oil into the tomato sauce. Tear the mozzarella into pieces and pat dry with paper towels. Wet cheese makes a soggy pizza.

Dust the counter with flour. Press the dough from the centre outward with your fingertips, leaving a 2cm border for the crust, then lift and stretch it over your knuckles into a 30cm round. Avoid a rolling pin as it knocks out the air.
Place the dough on baking paper. Spread the sauce thinly, keeping the border clear, and scatter over the mozzarella.
Slide the pizza with its paper onto the hot tray. Bake for 10–12 min, until the crust is puffed and charred in spots and the cheese is bubbling.
Top with torn basil and a drizzle of olive oil, rest for 1 min and slice.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Grease a 20cm square tin and line it with baking paper, leaving extra hanging over the sides so you can lift the brownies out.

Chop the chocolate and put it with the butter in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, with the bowl not touching the water. Stir for 4 min until smooth, then take off the heat and cool for 5 min.
Whisk the sugar into the chocolate mixture until glossy.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking for 30 seconds after each, then add the vanilla. The batter should thicken and turn shiny, which gives the crackly top.
Sift the flour, cocoa and salt over the bowl and fold in gently with a spatula until no streaks remain. Do not overmix.
Pour into the tin, spread level and tap it on the counter to remove air bubbles.
Bake for 25 min. A toothpick in the centre should come out with moist crumbs, not wet batter. The top should look set and crackly.
Cool in the tin for 30 min, lift out and cut into 9 squares with a warm knife. Dust with cocoa powder.
Use rice cooked and chilled for at least a few hours, ideally the day before. Break up any clumps with your fingers. Fresh hot rice turns mushy.
Prepare everything first because the cooking is fast: dice the carrot small, slice the beans, mince the garlic and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Heat a wok or large pan on high until it starts to smoke. Add 1 tbsp oil, the carrot and beans and stir-fry for 3 min. Add the peas and cook 1 min.
Push the vegetables to one side, add 1 tbsp oil and crack in the eggs. Scramble for 1 min until just set, then mix into the vegetables. Skip this step if you prefer it egg-free.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and white spring onion and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the rice, spread it out and press flat. Leave 1 min to toast, then toss. Repeat for 3 min until hot and some grains are crisp.
Pour the soy sauce around the edge of the pan rather than on the rice, add the sesame oil and pepper and toss for 1 min. Taste and add salt if needed.
Top with the green spring onion and sesame seeds and serve straight away.
Peel the mangoes and slice the flesh off the stone, aiming for about 300g. If using frozen mango, use it straight from the freezer for a thicker lassi.
Put the mango, yoghurt, milk, sugar and cardamom in a blender.
Blend on high for 1 min until completely smooth with no stringy bits.
Taste it. Add more sugar if the mango is sour, or a splash of milk if it is too thick.
Add the ice cubes and blend for 20 seconds until frothy and cold.
Pour into tall glasses, top with chopped pistachios and a pinch of cardamom and serve immediately.
